30.26.2.en: * The boiling of the bowels of the holy Church, as regards her, is the enduring of the violence of persecution... [The days of affliction prevented me]. The Church of the elect knows that she will suffer many evils in the last tribulation, but the days of affliction hinder her, because even in time of peace she bears within her the lives of the wicked with a burdened spirit.

30.26.4.en: I went mourning without the sun.

30.27.0.en: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation [28].

30.27.1.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that Job's speech here is the speech of every righteous man whose heart burns, not with the fire of the sun of trials, but with the fires of holy zeal and the sincere desire for the salvation of every soul. The believer will not rest until he finds all resting with him in the Lord, and enjoying with him the experience of the earnest of heaven! He cries out with the prophet Jeremiah, saying: "My bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart; my heart maketh a noise in me; I cannot hold my peace" (Jer 4:19).

30.27.2.en: * [I went in mourning garb (black) without provoking wrath, I stood up in the congregation and cried] [28]. Although this man had authority over his companions, inwardly he was offering to the Lord a secret sacrifice of a contrite heart, during his mourning. [The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart] (Ps 51:17)...

30.27.3.en: He was a witness against himself that in the midst of all those circumstances (of wealth, authority, and so on) he did not take his ease, but was in mourning. For to the saint who is still in a state of pilgrimage (in the world), everything, however full of prosperity, without the vision of God is utter poverty. For the elect, seeing everything, grieve that they do not see the Creator of all things, and to them all these things are exceedingly trivial compared with their deprivation of the appearing of the Supreme Being.

30.28.0.en: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls [29].

30.28.1.en: Job found no man to support him in his distress, even among his household, such as his wife or his relatives, so he counted the ravening wolves his brothers, living among them like a simple lamb. He also counted his friends like the ostriches, which have a beautiful appearance but are unable to fly like most birds.

30.28.2.en: We should not wonder that we live in a world that does not separate the righteous from the wicked, and does not cleanse the wheat from the chaff, until the hour comes in which the true separation will take place before the Almighty Judge.

30.28.3.en: * He says that I have fallen to the level of the birds or the ostriches. I no longer know my nature; my state has become no better than theirs. This is also what David said: "I am like an owl of the desert... I am as a sparrow alone upon the house top" (Ps 102:6-7).

30.28.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * [I was a brother to dragons, and a companion to ostriches] [29]. To what do the dragons refer but to the lives of those with evil minds? Of these it is also said through the prophet: [They snuffed up the wind like dragons] (Jer 14:6). All the wicked snuff up the wind like dragons, when they are swallowed up by evil thoughts of pride.

30.28.5.en: But what are we to understand by those who are indicated by the ostriches but lovers of display? For the ostrich has wings but does not fly; so all lovers of display have the appearance of holiness, but lack the goodness of holiness.

30.28.6.en: This also agrees with the words of blessed Job, who was of a level of endurance and steadfastness, a good man among the wicked. For there is no perfect man who is not gentle in the midst of the evils of his relatives. He who does not bear the evils of others with composure, with his longsuffering, bears witness of himself that he is very far from the fullness of goodness.

30.28.7.en: He who has not experienced the malice of Cain refuses to be "Abel."

30.28.8.en: For on the threshing floor the wheat lies under the pressure of the chaff... and the rose with its beautiful fragrance grows among the prickly thorns.

30.28.9.en: Noah's three sons were in the ark, but two continued in humility, and one in recklessness despised his father.

30.28.10.en: Abraham had two sons, one was righteous, and the other was a persecutor of his brother.

30.28.11.en: Isaac had two sons, one was saved in humility, and the second was cast out even before he was born.

30.28.12.en: Twelve sons were born to Jacob; of these one was sold in innocence, and the rest were the sellers of their brother through their wickedness.

30.28.13.en: Twelve disciples were chosen in the holy Church, but they did not remain without testing; one mingled among them, by whose persecution (of them) they were tried.

30.28.14.en: The righteous man cleaves to the evil of the sinner, as in the furnace straw is added to the gold in the fire: the straw burns, and the gold is refined. Truly they are good people who are able to hold fast to goodness even in the midst of the wicked.

30.28.15.en: It was said to the holy Church by the voice of the Bridegroom: "As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters" (Song 2:2). And so the Lord says to Ezekiel: [And you, son of man, have unbelievers and fallen ones about you, and you dwell among scorpions] (Ezek 2:6).

30.28.16.en: Peter glorified the life of blessed Lot, saying: "And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)" (2 Pet 2:7-8).

30.28.17.en: Paul glorifies the life of his disciples, and by glorifying them he strengthens them, saying: "In the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world; holding forth the word of life" (Phil 2:15-16). So also through John the angel of the church of Pergamos bears witness to that in the words: "I know... where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith" (Rev 2:13)

30.29.0.en: My skin is black (turned black) upon me, and my bones are burned with heat (the fever in me) [30].

30.29.1.en: In referring to the Church, Pope Gregory (the Great) sees the sorrow of the Church over the weak souls whose skin the sun of tribulations burns and whose bones it scorches, so that she counts what befalls them as befalling her, since they are members of the Church.

30.29.2.en: * [My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with the heat within me] [30]... By the skin he indicates the weak, those who serve in her for an outward benefit. And the bones represent the strong, since through them the whole body is held together.

30.29.3.en: The weak in the Church fall away from steadfastness in the faith, either by the temptation of money or by being broken by persecutions. And after their fall they themselves persecute her, so the Church suffers from the blackness of her skin.

30.29.4.en: [And my bones are dried up with heat]: the strongest bone of the holy Church, Paul, was burned, and dried up with anxiety for others, when he said concerning some who had fallen: "Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not?" (2 Cor 11:29). So the skin turned black and the bones dried up with heat, because the weak leap toward evil, and the strong are tormented by the fire of their zeal.

30.29.6.en: * To what shall we compare Paul, who groans daily for every man in this world, for every nation and city, for every soul? His resolve was stronger than iron and firmer than steel, so with what words shall we describe this spirit?!

30.29.7.en: * What a wondrous feeling in the shepherd! Others fall and he says: I affirm my grief. Others stumble and he says: The fires of my sufferings burn!

30.29.8.en: Would that all to whom the leadership of the rational flock has been entrusted would imitate this, and not show themselves to be less than the shepherd who for many years cares for an irrational flock.

30.29.9.en: For in the case of the irrational flock no appreciable harm occurs even if there is neglect, but in our case, if one sheep perishes or is devoured, the harm will be very grave and terrifying, and the punishment unspeakable; above all this, since the Lord had first endured the shedding of His blood for it, what excuse can this man offer, who allows himself to neglect the one for whom the Lord cared and for whose sake He gave every effort on His part for the care of the flock?

30.30.0.en: St. John Chrysostom My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep [31].

30.30.1.en: St. Augustine sees that Job here looks to the Holy Spirit who strikes the strings of the human soul and makes of it a harp and a pipe; the soul melts with love for humanity in the Lord. Man spends his life grieving for every suffering soul and weeping with those who weep. This is the wisdom of God working in man, so that he shares the feelings of all, and in this he feels a surpassing peace while grieving for others.

30.30.2.en: And Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that the believer is like a string on a lute or harp: if it is struck very lightly it gives no sound, and if it is struck hard it causes a disturbance. Therefore it befits man to walk in moderation in everything: in his asceticism he should not exaggerate lest he destroy his vitality, nor abandon asceticism altogether so that he cannot control his body.

30.30.3.en: We are different strings on the harp of God, working together, and a joyful symphony comes forth that God receives as an acceptable sacrifice of praise and thanksgiving, pleasing to Him. By this the believer enjoys the heavenly life as a communal life in the Lord; each member by himself feels the touches of the hand of God playing upon him, but with the same hand He strikes the other strings in wondrous harmony and concord!

30.30.4.en: * It is hard for us to doubt, I think, that Job in this expression means the Holy Spirit.

30.30.5.en: The subject of the discussion is wisdom, where it comes to men from; it does not come from many years, but the Holy Spirit who dwells in mortals, and the breath of the Almighty, is what teaches...

30.30.6.en: It is perfectly clear that he is not speaking of the spirit of man in the expression "the Spirit who is in mortals." He wanted to show from where men receive wisdom, for it is not from themselves... In the same way in another passage in the same book he says: [The understanding of my lips shall not meditate purity. The divine Spirit that formed me, and the breath of the Almighty teaches me] (cf. Job 33:3-4) LXX.

30.30.7.en: St. Augustine * "My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep" [31]. Let it be considered that if the string of the harp is struck very lightly it gives no sound, and if it is struck with great force it produces a harsh sound. So the virtue of asceticism becomes altogether nothing if a man does not discipline his body as far as he can. But it is wrongly used if a man wears out his body beyond what it can bear. For by asceticism the deficiencies of the body are consumed, not the body itself, and it befits each one to control himself with exact discipline, so that the body does not grow proud and sin, and yet is sustained to practice righteousness. The great preacher says: "Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth" (Col 3:5). And yet he wrote to the preacher who was very dear to him: "Use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities" (1 Tim 5:23).

30.30.10.en: * I often look at my life and see that it has passed quickly without fruit.

30.30.11.en: I wanted to bear witness to You each time that time passed over me.

30.30.12.en: But my soul is bitter, for I see no spiritual fruits in my life and my service!

30.30.13.en: Who removes the spirit of despair from me, except Your cross, O Giver of hope!

30.30.14.en: Let me cling to You, and carry me on Your arms, and let my soul be assured by You, O Savior of souls from corruption!

30.30.15.en: * Many mock me even in my old age!

30.30.16.en: They reflect what is in their hearts of want, hunger and shame, and pour it upon my soul to shatter it.

30.30.17.en: But You are my heavenly bread, my satisfaction and my glory!

30.30.18.en: Fix my eyes upon You, that I may rise above the dunghill from which I suffer.

30.30.19.en: * Around me have gathered those who have not tasted the truth nor been satisfied by Your grace, and behold, they mock me.

30.30.20.en: They went out against You as against a thief, and behold, they do the same work with Your Church!

30.30.21.en: Grant me that my soul be not troubled!

30.30.22.en: * They left the city of God with all its blessings.

30.30.23.en: Instead of returning to it, they gloat over the suffering men of God.

30.30.24.en: * They went out to the wastelands and the wildernesses, depriving themselves of the divine planting and the waters of the Holy Spirit; they thought themselves strong, and came to mock the divine plants, the wondrous vineyard of God!

30.30.25.en: * Why does my soul groan at the mockery of the world.

30.30.27.en: Your sufferings and the shame of Your cross and Your death for me are my true comfort!

30.30.28.en: Who is worthy to share with You in Your glorious shame?

30.30.29.en: Who is qualified to carry Your cross with You?

30.30.30.en: * In the distress of my soul I see that You have loosed the reins for those who trouble me; You seem as one who aims arrows against me.

30.30.31.en: But You, who are all love, turn my bitterness into sweetness.

30.30.32.en: You turn the troubles of my opponents into eternal glories.

30.30.33.en: You leave them to mock with their tongues, to pour out accusations against me.

30.30.34.en: And to practice injustice as though without restraint!

30.30.35.en: And in all this Your eyes are upon me, taking pity on me!

30.30.36.en: You are my salvation and my glory!

30.30.37.en: * When I fall under sufferings, You are revealed before me, O You who suffered for me, and I forget my sufferings in the sight of You that gladdens my heart.

30.30.38.en: And my lamentation is turned into a heavenly song and unceasing rejoicing.

30.30.39.en: * The deceiver has no work but to lead me astray from the truth.

30.30.40.en: He thinks he is cutting off my way, so that I shall not pass into the Kingdom.

30.30.41.en: How foolish he is. You are the Way that no power can hide from me.

30.30.42.en: He seeks my destruction, and has not realized that You are my almighty Savior.

30.30.43.en: * The enemy moves toward me as in a storm to destroy me.

30.30.44.en: He thinks he is crushing me like a stone under a wide stone crusher.

30.30.45.en: He has not realized that You are the cornerstone, joining me by You to the heavenly temple!

30.30.46.en: There is no power that can crush me while I am in Your hands!

30.30.47.en: * My life has become like a passing wind or a cloud that soon vanishes.

30.30.48.en: It has become as though without aim or taste!

30.30.49.en: It has dried up completely like a tree without life or fruit.

30.30.50.en: The night rushed upon me, and began to gnaw my bones.

30.30.51.en: My veins within me know no rest.

30.30.52.en: I wrapped myself in sufferings like a garment clinging to me.

30.30.53.en: I was cast into the midst of the mire.

30.30.54.en: And my life turned into dust and ashes.

30.30.55.en: * My life has lost all stability and security.

30.30.56.en: My eyes have turned to the grave, as a house in which every man settles!

30.30.57.en: The light has turned to darkness for me.

30.30.58.en: My bowels within me have melted from boiling.

30.30.59.en: I no longer have anyone to comfort me, nor anyone to share my sufferings.

30.30.60.en: I have become a brother to the savage wolves, and to the ostriches that cannot fly!

30.30.61.en: I no longer play on the harp of my soul a song or a hymn.

30.30.62.en: Rather, my whole being has turned into a harp that plays perpetual laments!

30.30.63.en: * This is my lamentation; who can comfort me but You?

30.30.64.en: Who can raise me from the grave except the One who rose from the dead?

30.30.65.en: Who lifts me from the dunghill but the Heavenly One who by His love came down to me?

30.30.66.en: Who gives my life taste except the One who turns bitterness into sweetness; my lamentation does not shatter my soul, but gives me hope in You, O Gladdener of hearts!
